structure_evidence.object_linked_access:
I represent a green cross at left, a red square at right, a yellow triangle at upper, and an ambiguous object at lower with no identified color or shape. Attention is currently focused on the left object, which is also the most recoverable now; its recoverability declines over subsequent steps. The right object is identified but less recoverable now than left. The upper object is identifiable but less available than left or right. The lower location has little identified information and the lowest recoverability. If I redirect attention in View A, the model predicts the next selection will go to the location I command (commands map to the commanded location), so allocation would change to that object; its future recoverability is given by that object's recorded one- and two-step recoverability values.

View B:
I represent a blue square at right, a red triangle at upper, a yellow circle at left, and a green cross at lower. Attention is currently on the right object, while the upper object is most recoverable now. Commanding different locations does not change the predicted next allocation: the model predicts selection will move to the lower location regardless, and its recoverability values are lower than the presently most recoverable upper.
